text: Your Black Friday deal could be cheaper in January.
One TV was cheaper on 134 days after the sale.
So is the deal real?
Consumer Group Witch tracked 175 products
at eight big retailers for a whole year.
83% were the same price or cheaper at some other time.
Shocking.
Truly, I'm shocked.
So how does an ordinary price look like a deal?
The was price.
Discounts are often measured from a price the item rarely sold at.
Add a countdown clock and you stop checking.
And the trick doesn't stop on Friday.
Prices often drop again after the sale.
That TV later sold for 27% less.
That's the mirage.
The discount is measured from a price nobody paid.
The real test is the price history, not the percent off.
